findings.title: R2 acquisition second read can adopt an unreceipted bucket
findings.case: In create mode, initial R2 preflight GET returns absent. Between preflight and the acquisition-loop GET, another actor creates the same-name bucket. The second GET returns that bucket; line 381 continues based solely on its name, without resource-storage.done or an acknowledged creation POST.
findings.impact: Creation proceeds using a resource whose ownership was not established by the protected operation. This bypasses the corrected initial no-name-adoption check.
findings.required: Require the exact protected creation proof on every create-mode existing-bucket path, including a bucket appearing after preflight; preserve read-only uncertain-result reconciliation and no destructive compensation. Add the precise interleaving to the existing focused fixture.

findings.title: Restore conflates latest-upload material provenance with active/resume traffic
cases: Promote A; upload B without promotion; request restore using the exact current B upload receipt. currentPrior accepts B as latest plus an unchanged deployment snapshot, but does not require B to be active. Resume then promotes B at 100%, so a data restore implicitly activates pending code instead of preserving the previous active code/traffic state.

Restore with resume uploads a newer quarantine version Q, then activates prior version P and returns P with the new sourceState. Versions remain ordered Q,P. A subsequent legitimate reconcile/upload/rotate/rollback/restore using the exact returned receipt fails currentPrior's latest-version-equals-prior.version requirement (and the later redundant latest check).
findings.impact: Recovery can silently promote an unpromoted artifact, and even its reported successful resume does not yield a usable current lifecycle receipt.
findings.required: Represent and verify latest-upload/credential provenance separately from a supported explicit active/resume topology. Refuse unpromoted or ambiguous recovery targets before mutation; never relax stale-rotation/material checks. Return a receipt that permits a subsequent legitimate lifecycle operation after quarantine/resume. Cover both cases in existing focused fixtures.
findings.evidence: Actual frozen source and actual fixture inspection. The current restore fixtures start from an uploaded-not-promoted create result and assert final activation only, so K4 PASS8 is non-discriminating for these schedules. No extra reproducer was run.

findings.title: Rollback security closure omits bound Durable Object enforcement
findings.case: The actual successful package has 319 security barrier pins but excludes DecisionRing.ts, LearnStats.ts and RegionTrend.ts. securityClosure intentionally does not traverse src/index.ts imports. Runtime DO calls do not form static caller-import edges. A retained historical artifact differing only in DecisionRing's tombstone/retention enforcement can have identical current barrier pins and pass rollback compatibility.
findings.impact: Rollback can reintroduce older code that ignores the still-current KV/R2/DO erasure or retention barriers. DecisionRing.current directly reads erased_at and filters records, so its implementation is itself an enforcement dependency.
findings.required: Include every bound DO/background enforcement implementation and its real transitive dependencies in rollback compatibility, accounting for runtime binding boundaries. Add a historical-artifact discriminator where only that enforcement implementation changes; keep genuinely compatible non-security rollback working.
findings.evidence: Actual safe package manifest a99241a7d68eec42c2b40d623b3bc21607082d825e6c3f31f701d896001bd23e and actual DecisionRing source, not merely a synthetic manifest. No extra reproducer was run.
